title: Preregistered Paired Evaluation of a Composed LLM→Validator→Emulator Workflow for NetOps Intent Translation
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired study (PR-CW-2026-001) comparing (A) LLM-only configuration generation versus (B) a composed workflow (LLM → retrieval-constrained templating → deterministic validator(s) → emulator replay) on 200 NetOps intents (IPv4 routing, ACLs, basic switching, topology). Primary estimand: per-intent difference in emulator-detected unsafe/executable faults. Complete paired analysis (n=199) found baseline unsafe rate 0/199 and guarded unsafe rate 0/199 (paired McNemar exact two-sided p=1.0; 95% CI for paired difference 0.0–0.0). One paired item was removed per preregistered technical-failure rules. Confirmatory conclusion: within this preregistered domain and corpus, the composed workflow did not reduce emulator-detected unsafe executions relative to LLM-only because the baseline generation produced no emulator-detected unsafe cases. We report all preregistered artifacts, execution manifests, and limitations (single-domain synthetic corpus, single hosted LLM provider recorded in execution/model_configuration.json, validator coverage constraints).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being applied to NetOps tasks (intent→configuration). Prior work emphasizes both promise and safety risks (hallucination, unsafe actions) and recommends generate–validate–repair or tool-augmented architectures. We asked: does a reproducible composed workflow that injects retrieval-constrained templating and deterministic validation before emulator replay reduce executable/unsafe faults compared with LLM-only generation on the same intents? Contributions: (1) preregistration PR-CW-2026-001 and full execution manifest; (2) a paired experiment (n=200 intents, paired treatments) using hosted LLM calls, retrieval+templating, Batfish/NetKAT validators, and Mininet emulator; (3) complete confirmatory analysis and full artifact release.
sections.related_work: Work motivating the pipeline includes surveys and systems advocating validator-assisted NetOps and bounded agentic workflows (e.g., NetOps/AIOps surveys and Batfish operational lessons). We positioned the study as an operationally focused proof-of-concept rather than a multi-model benchmark; closest prior references used in preregistration: Large Language Models for Agentic NetOps and AIOps (arXiv), TopoIntent (arXiv), and Batfish evolution (OpenAlex records listed in cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistered plan (PR-CW-2026-001) and frozen procedures: paired within-intent design on a deterministically sampled corpus (200 intents stratified by complexity: simple/moderate/complex). Treatments: (A) LLM-only generation; (B) composed workflow = LLM → local retrieval-index templates → slot-filling → deterministic syntax checks → validator pipeline (Batfish + NetKAT cross-check where applicable) → Mininet emulator replay (executable/script application). Inclusion/exclusion, retry policy (max 3 attempts), seeds, contamination checks (retrieval snapshot checksum), and analysis (primary: paired McNemar exact) were fixed before execution. All prompts, model outputs, logs, and artifact hashes were recorded; key manifests are in execution_manifest and analysis artifacts referenced below.
sections.results: Execution completed as preregistered (execution_manifest.status=COMPLETED). Planned pairs: 200. Complete paired count used in primary analysis: 199 (one pair excluded per preregistered technical-failure rule). Confirmatory outcome: baseline emulator-detected unsafe executions = 0/199; guarded/composed workflow emulator-detected unsafe executions = 0/199. Paired McNemar exact (two-sided) p=1.0. Bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% CI for paired absolute difference = [0.0, 0.0]. Secondary analyses per preregistration (fault-count comparisons, validator coverage estimates) are provided in the released artifacts; no emulator-detected unsafe faults occurred in either treatment for the analyzed corpus.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: the composed validator+emulator pipeline did not show an improvement over LLM-only generation because the baseline generation produced no emulator-detected unsafe cases in this corpus. Possible reasons: (1) the synthetic/publicly-derived intent corpus and constrained NetOps domain may be easier than open production tickets; (2) retrieval templates, grammar constraints, or prompt design used across both treatments may have biased baseline toward safe outputs; (3) validators/emulator may share semantic alignment with the task domain such that many LLM proposals were already emulator-executable. Exploratory signals (validator false-negative estimation, per-stratum behavior) are available in the artifacts but are explicitly exploratory per the preregistration.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered, fully documented paired study (PR-CW-2026-001) over a 200-intent NetOps corpus, we found no evidence that the composed LLM→retrieval→validator→emulator workflow reduced emulator-detected unsafe executions relative to LLM-only generation because the LLM-only baseline produced zero unsafe emulator outcomes on the tested corpus. The result is narrowly scoped; further work should test broader, noisier, or adversarial intent distributions and multiple LLM providers and validator implementations to assess generality.

limitations: Domain and corpus scope: the corpus was a synthetic/publicly-derived intent set limited to IPv4 routing, ACLs, basic switching, and topology operations; results do not generalize to broader or adversarial intent distributions.
Single-hosted LLM provider: calls used a single hosted LLM provider (identifier recorded in execution/model_configuration.json); results do not imply cross-model generality.

Validator/emulator coverage: Batfish/NetKAT and Mininet approximate operational behavior but do not fully capture all production semantics; validator false negatives remain possible (discovery set used to estimate coverage).

Potential corpus easiness: zero unsafe emulator outcomes in the baseline suggest the tested corpus may be insufficiently challenging to reveal differences; real-world tickets may produce different behavior.
Sample exclusions: one planned pair was excluded per preregistered technical-failure rules; sensitivity ITT analyses are available in artifacts.
No human-operator comparison: we did not compare automated outputs to human operator performance in this run.
Not a production evaluation: the study is a controlled, proof-of-concept experiment and not a deployment test.
